name: poll_origin_basic
kind: survey: (A) how long a plain try_wait on an incomplete phase holds its warp before it returns false, by what else runs on the SM and by what the polling warp does between calls; (B) on which pc the hardware books a poll wait when the first instruction waiting for the poll's result is 6, 10 or 14 instructions behind the poll, and when a shared-memory load lies between; installs nothing
why: placement v4, last addendum: origin_hold_cycles = 3877 was a misreading (per wait the hardware holds the inline reader 7754 cycles in u.pollcute.k1024, while s.mbar_trywait_fail returns after 3876 per call), and the reach of 4 records for the wait origin had no measurement. Full GPU (full-place4, points of per-pc error inside mbarrier-poll sites, h100 / b300): cap 0.6 / 3.0, first waiter 5-16 behind the poll 2.75 / 3.27, inline poll kept apart from its loop by a rejected instruction 0.38 / 1.93.
data_seen_before_freezing: placement_basic v1 / v2, placement v1-v4 and their addenda; the poll_residual analysis (full-place4, full-place4-o7754, full-place4-oinf) and the traces of 19 full-GPU cases (first-waiter distances 6, 8, 8, 9 and none; LDS, MUFU, LDL, P2R, LDC between the polls).
sync_basic v1 (3876 cycles per call, s.mbar_trywait_fail, 1 and 4 warps per CTA all polling), v4 (u.handoff.k1024: one false result per wait of 9340 cycles).
No run of the cells below.

probe.chain: As placement_basic: hand-written PTX (probe/t.timeout.<cfg>.ptx, u.pollfar4.ptx, u.pollfar8.ptx, u.pollfar14.ptx, u.pollfar.lds.ptx), ptxas -O3 -> nvdisasm loop gate -> ptx_runner; cells in sync_basic/cells.tsv, suite rows set poll_origin_basic; build dir $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/poll_origin_basic/<device>/build, run root $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/poll_origin_basic/<device>; direct runs (launches 0-2 kept as u32 dumps), capture, two reference passes, replay with build 2e705118.

cells.A: t.timeout.<cfg>, one CTA per SM, n = 12 calls, k = 32768: warp 0 polls a barrier that never completes: clock, try_wait, branch on its result, clock; the 12 differences are words 4-15 of each thread. cfg: alone (1 warp per CTA); arr (1 warp; the polling warp arrives on a second barrier of count 1000 in front of every call); gap (1 warp; a delay loop of 516 iterations in front of every call); idle1 (2 warps, the second returns at once); busy1 (2 warps, the second runs a delay loop of k iterations, longer than the 12 calls); busy1.gap; busy1.arr; busy3 (4 warps, three in the delay loop).
cells.B: u.pollfar4.k64, u.pollfar8.k64, u.pollfar14.k64, u.pollfar8.k1024: u.pollcute with 4 / 8 / 14 shift-xor instructions between each inline try_wait and the branch on its result (after ptxas the branch is 6 / 10 / 14 instructions behind the TRYWAIT on both architectures). u.pollfar.lds.k64: a shared-memory load of the thread's own word and an add of it between them (TRYWAIT, LDS, ISETP, IMAD.IADD, BRA).

readings: A: per cell and device the 12 per-call durations (median over SMs, spread), launches 1 and 2. B: per cell, per-warp cycles of class long_scoreboard on every pc of both poll sites from both passes, normalised PER WAIT (each site is run by one warp of the pair: per-warp average times 2), and the replay's barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK cycles on the same pcs; the direct runs' out-of-line polls per wait.

questions_before_data.A1: Is the hold 3876 in every cfg and every call, or about 7754 in some (which: a busy second warp, a gap in front of the call, an arrive in front of the call), or does it vary from call to call (a free-running period)?
questions_before_data.A2: From A1: which value bounds the time a wait stays on the inline reader in u.pollcute.k1024 (7754 per wait) -- one long time-out, or the inline call's time-out plus the first out-of-line call's?
questions_before_data.B1: Far cells: is the whole wait long_scoreboard on the branch 6 / 10 / 14 behind the TRYWAIT, nothing on the instructions between and nothing in the retry loop (k64)? At k1024: the same per-wait hold on that branch as in u.pollcute.k1024?
questions_before_data.B2: lds cell: wait on the branch (4 behind), on the LDS's reader, or elsewhere?

install: Nothing. The installation protocol placement v5 takes the hold value, the reach and the treatment of instructions between the polls from the addendum.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its data is seen.

addenda.when: 2026-11-21, run poll_origin_basic (clone stall-attribution-45, commit 80f53add; jobs mechver-porg1-h100 / -b300; roots $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/poll_origin_basic/{h100,b300}); 13 cells per device, direct values right, captured, two reference passes rc 0, replayed with 2e705118
addenda.text: A (direct clocks, launches 1 and 2, every SM, 12 calls each). One plain try_wait on a phase that never completes returns after 7760-7769 cycles clock to clock in EVERY cell and every call on both devices: alone 7764, arr 7767, gap 7769, idle1 7764, busy1 7760-7764, busy1.gap 7765-7769, busy1.arr 7763-7765, busy3 7760-7764; spread over SMs 0-4. A1: no dependence on a second warp, on a gap or on an arrive in front of the call, no call-to-call variation: one time-out. With the poll window's own instructions (clock read 6 cycles in front of the TRYWAIT, branch stall behind it) the false result is released 7757 cycles after the TRYWAIT's issue; the same 7757 follows from the reader holds: u.pollcute.k1024 7754 with the reader 3 cycles behind the poll, u.pollfar8.k1024 7730-7734 with the reader 27 cycles behind it. A2: the 7754 per wait of u.pollcute.k1024 is the inline call's time-out alone. The 3876 `per call` of sync_basic v1 (s.mbar_trywait_fail) does not hold: that kernel's cycles over its 64 iterations give 3896, i.e. the iteration count or the unrolling was misread there by a factor of two; the clocks of this run are per call. The 1.96 microsecond time-out quoted since is 3.92 microseconds (7757 cycles, the same count on both devices). B (per-warp long_scoreboard, both passes, PER WAIT = per-warp average x 2; out-of-line polls per wait from the direct runs). k = 64, 0.00 out-of-line polls: the whole wait is on the branch that waits for the poll's barrier, whatever its distance: u.pollfar4 811-818 on the BRA 6 behind the TRYWAIT (site A) and 3 behind (site B; ptxas moved fillers in front of the poll there); u.pollfar8 810 / 789 on the BRA 10 / 7 behind; u.pollfar14 788 / 767 on the BRA 14 / 12 behind; b300 the same pcs with 776-820, 780-788, 767-788; nothing on the instructions between, nothing in the retry loop. B1 at k = 1024 (1.00 out-of-line poll per wait): 7730-7734 on the far BRA (h100), 7727-7731 (b300), then 1707-1733 (1222-1710 b300) on NANOSLEEP.SYNCS and 22-25 on the loop's BRA. B2, u.pollfar.lds.k64: 783 / 764 (h100), 780 / 757 (b300) on the BRA 4 / 3 behind the TRYWAIT; the LDS's reader carries its own short_scoreboard (1.3 per iteration) and nothing of the poll wait. The replay (2e705118) has that cell's wait in the retry loop: the LDS between the inline poll and the loop's polls keeps the inline poll out of the fold. Open: the leaf synchronization.mbarrier.trywait_timeout carries cycles = 0 from the crossings cell (a try_wait that did not suspend, period 28); that cell and these disagree and the difference between them is not looked at here. Nothing is installed from these readings.

addenda.when: 2026-11-22, the two earlier measurements that disagreed with the 7757-cycle time-out, looked at (listings and control words of their probes, their own data; no new run)
addenda.text: They do not disagree; each measured something else, and one sentence of the addendum above is corrected. (1) crossings trywait_timeout cell (source of the leaf's cycles = 0: `period of a try_wait loop 28 cycles = that of test_wait: the hardware does not suspend an unsatisfied try_wait beyond its issue`). Its probe never reads the try_wait's result: the SASS is SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT PT, [R4+UR4], RZ with destination PT and no write barrier (control word: write barrier 7), and no instruction of the loop waits for it (h100 and b300 listings, $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/crossings/h100-r2/trywait_timeout/build/sass/trywait.sass). A try_wait whose result nobody reads holds nobody, so the loop runs at the speed of test_wait. What the cell shows is that the poll instruction itself is not suspended; it does not show that there is no time-out. Its release cell (TRYWAIT P2 with write barrier 0, read by a branch) has the same structure as the cells here. The older value it replaced, 7892 cycles for an `abandoned suspending try_wait` (hopper-prototype), fits 7757 plus a loop. (2) sync_basic v1, `3876 cycles per call` (s.mbar_trywait_fail). The addendum above says the iteration count or the unrolling was misread; precisely: ptxas unrolls that loop four times, the first three TRYWAITs (write barriers 0, 1, 2) are issued back to back and the fourth (barrier 0) behind the reader of the first. Per-pc samples: the reader of the first carries 124025 cycles of long_scoreboard over 16 trips = 7752 per trip, the readers of the second and third 35 each (their time-outs ran concurrently and had expired), the reader of the fourth 7743. Two holds of about 7750 per four calls = 3876 per call on average. So: a try_wait's result is pending from its issue until the phase completes or 7757 cycles have passed, each poll counting from its own issue, and it holds only instructions that wait for its dependency barrier. CONSEQUENCES, none installed here: the leaf's cycles = 0 is what the engine charges a failed poll that is still in the replayed stream; on hardware a failed poll whose result is read holds its reader 7757 cycles, but the failed polls of a traced stream are mostly an effect of tracing (the fold drops them), so whether and how to charge the remaining ones is a timing question for a later protocol. The description of the crossings source in the mechanism tree says more than its probe shows (`does not suspend ... -> cycles = 0, measured`); it is left as it is with this addendum as the correction, because changing the tree's sources needs a formal build.
